task.description: Re-gate WF-02 Step 1b for REQ-038 on branch feature/WF02-REQ-038 (commit 915c2ff) after CODE-DESIGNER's rework of the single blocking FAIL from step-01b-code-design-validator.json (AC7's plain-path integration gap for hasPastCheckIn -> decideRegistrationOutcome's inviteSatisfied field). Re-read docs/agents/design/REQ-038.md's current full text (specifically updated ss2.2 and the file-change manifest, and the AC7 row in ss8), re-read apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's full current registerForEvent (lines 119-263) to independently re-verify the claimed insertion point, confirmed git diff 92d35ce..915c2ff -- docs/agents/design/REQ-038.md to scope-check the rework touched only ss2.2/manifest/AC7-row and left every other previously-passed section byte-identical.
acceptance_criteria: AC7 (past check-in -> admitted without code; no past check-in -> refused with onward path; derivation is a query) must now have a concrete, unambiguous integration point in registerForEvent with no external signature change and no unedited call site left inconsistent.

result.summary: The rework closes the one blocking gap. ss2.2 now states, with no TBD/deferral language, that hasPastCheckIn(tx, userId) is called from inside registerForEvent's own existing transaction -- a new internal step inserted after the existing event-row lock (step 2, which yields event.requiresInvite off the locked row) and before the existing decideRegistrationOutcome call (step 6), only when event.requiresInvite is true; when false, inviteSatisfied is passed as false unconditionally with no query run. registerForEvent's external signature (db, userId, eventId, evaluationTime) is unchanged, so handlers/registration.ts's register:<eventId> call site needs no edit -- independently re-verified against the actual current file: userId is already a parameter (line 121), event.requiresInvite is read and passed at line 181 exactly as the design quotes it ('requiresInvite: event.requiresInvite,'), the event lock (step 2) spans lines 126-144, and the decideRegistrationOutcome call (step 6) spans lines 176-188, so the stated insertion window is real and sits strictly between them; the intervening steps (existingAdmission read, admittedCount, seatsLeft) neither depend on nor are depended on by hasPastCheckIn, so the window's imprecision about exact sub-step placement has no effect on correctness. TOCTOU reasoning re-verified as sound: computing inviteSatisfied inside the same locked transaction that reads existingAdmission/admittedCount/event.status and performs the write closes exactly the gap option (a) (handler-side, pre-transaction read) would have left open, consistent with every other input to that same decision already being read inside the lock. registerForEvent is now correctly named in the top-of-document file-change manifest, and the AC7 row in ss8 cites the exact call-site resolution. Scope check via git diff 92d35ce..915c2ff -- docs/agents/design/REQ-038.md confirms the rework touched only the manifest bullet, ss2.2, and the AC7 table row -- every other section independently verified in the first pass (FR-4/AC8 resolution at ss2.4/ss8, the identity-leakage adversarial trace for AC2/design question 1, the atomic used_count increment at ss3.1 steps 5-6/10, decideRegistrationOutcome's byte-for-byte minimal-diff claim at ss1.2, hasPastCheckIn's purity/no-cache property at ss2.1, the i_ deep-link consent-gate reuse at ss4.2/ss4.3) is byte-identical to the version that already passed those checks and was not re-litigated here. Gate checklist re-confirmed for the whole document: every AC maps to a concrete design element (ss8), no TBD/deferral language anywhere, all new props/types (RegistrationDecisionInput.inviteSatisfied, InviteRedemptionOutcome, InviteCodeValidationInput/Result, StartPayload's new invite member) are fully specified interfaces/signatures, no color/spacing/typography token references appear anywhere in this bot-only design (correctly out of scope per ss9, consistent with the first pass), and every one of the document's 16 fenced code blocks is a bare interface/type/function-signature declaration with no function body, no if/comparison/arithmetic statement -- verified by re-scanning all 16 blocks, none introduced by this rework contain a body.
